Legend

1. **[^](#cite_ref-8)**  Agreement between the two clubs rather than the two leagues
2. **[^](#cite_ref-9)**  There was no formal arrangement in place between the two leagues regarding the staging of the World Series, so the Giants owner [John T. Brush](/wiki/John_T._Brush "John T. Brush") refused to play against a team from what he considered an inferior league.
3. **[^](#cite_ref-10)**  Had the series been played, it would have been the [Boston Americans (AL)](/wiki/1904_Boston_Americans_season "1904 Boston Americans season") vs the [New York Giants (NL)](/wiki/1904_New_York_Giants_season "1904 New York Giants season")
4. **[^](#cite_ref-11)**  Formal agreement established between the two leagues to make the World Series into an annual event
5. **[^](#cite_ref-12)** The 1967 series marked the first time that the [Commissioner's Trophy](/wiki/Commissioner%27s_Trophy_(MLB) "Commissioner's Trophy (MLB)") was presented to the World Series-winning team.

* [**V**](#ref_BestOf9V) The 1903, 1919, 1920, and 1921 World Series were in a [best-of-nine format](/wiki/Best-of-nine_format "Best-of-nine format") (carried by the first team to win five games).
* [**T**](#ref_TieGameT) The 1907, 1912, and 1922 World Series each included one [tied game](/wiki/Tie_(draw) "Tie (draw)").
* [**A**](#ref_AmericanA) The Brewers were in the American League from [1969](/wiki/1969_Seattle_Pilots_season "1969 Seattle Pilots season") to [1997](/wiki/1997_Milwaukee_Brewers_season "1997 Milwaukee Brewers season"), after which they moved to the National League.[[8]](#cite_note-13)
* [**N**](#ref_NationalN) The Astros were in the National League from [1962](/wiki/1962_Houston_Colt_.45s_season "1962 Houston Colt .45s season") to [2012](/wiki/2012_Houston_Astros_season "2012 Houston Astros season"), after which they moved to the American League.

Alcaraz made his debut in the [main draw](/wiki/Main_draw_(tennis) "Main draw (tennis)") of a major as a [qualifier](/wiki/Qualifier_(tennis) "Qualifier (tennis)") at the [2021 Australian Open](/wiki/2021_Australian_Open "2021 Australian Open"). He was the youngest man to qualify for the tournament since [Novak Djokovic](/wiki/Novak_Djokovic "Novak Djokovic") in 2005.[[45]](#cite_note-:023-46) As the main draw was postponed due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), Alcaraz played the [Great Ocean Road Open](/wiki/2021_Great_Ocean_Road_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2021 Great Ocean Road Open – Singles") in early February, where he was defeated by [Thiago Monteiro](/wiki/Thiago_Monteiro_(tennis) "Thiago Monteiro (tennis)").[[46]](#cite_note-47) In his first main draw match at the Australian Open, Alcaraz defeated fellow qualifier [Botic van de Zandschulp](/wiki/Botic_van_de_Zandschulp "Botic van de Zandschulp") in straight sets. He was the only teenager in the draw to progress past the first round, and the first person born in 2003 to win a match at a major.[[45]](#cite_note-:023-46) In the second round, Alcaraz was defeated by [Mikael Ymer](/wiki/Mikael_Ymer "Mikael Ymer").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/Amaryllis-wiki.JPG/250px-Amaryllis-wiki.JPG)](/wiki/File:Amaryllis-wiki.JPG)

Single *Hippeastrum*

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Hippeastrum.JPG/250px-Hippeastrum.JPG)](/wiki/File:Hippeastrum.JPG)

Double *Hippeastrum*

*Hippeastrum* [hybrids](/wiki/Hybrid_(biology) "Hybrid (biology)") and [cultivars](/wiki/Cultivars "Cultivars") are valued for their large ornamental flowers, particularly for indoor cultivation during the [Northern Hemisphere](/wiki/Northern_Hemisphere "Northern Hemisphere") winter. The larger the bulb, the more flowers it will produce. The largest bulbs measure 14 to 16 inches (36 to 41 cm) in circumference and will produce three or more [scapes](/wiki/Scape_(botany) "Scape (botany)") (flower stems) with four or more blooms each. The commonest bulbs measure 10+1⁄2 to 12+1⁄2 inches (27 to 32 cm) with two scapes with four to six flowers each depending on the cultivar. Some bulbs put up two flower scapes at the same time; others may wait several weeks between blooms and sometimes the second scape will have only two or three flowers rather than the usual four. A bulb needs to produce large, healthy leaves in the summer growing season before it can send up a scape the following year. Bulbs are often described by the country of origin of the bulb producers, since they may have different characteristics, e.g. 'Dutch Amaryllis', 'South African Amarylllis'. Dutch bulbs usually produce flowers first, then, after they have finished blooming (hysteranthous), the plant will begin growing leaves. Bulbs from the South African growers usually put up a scape and leaves at the same time (synanthous).[[93]](#cite_note-ps-95)

Of the many hybrids, the best known are those producing flowers with red, pink, salmon, orange and white colors. Other flower colors include yellow and pale green with variations on these including multicolor

fanoutqa_009041.x:
List of longest-reigning monarchs :: Monarchs of sovereign states with verifiable reigns by exact date :: part 01 :: chunk_0001
The following are the 25 longest-reigning monarchs of states who were internationally recognised as sovereign for most or all of their reign. [Roman emperors](/wiki/List_of_Roman_emperors "List of Roman emperors") [Constantine VIII](/wiki/Constantine_VIII "Constantine VIII") and [Basil II](/wiki/Basil_II "Basil II"), reigning for 66 years in total (962–1028) and for 65 years in total (960–1025) respectively, are not included, because for part of those periods they reigned only nominally as junior co-emperors alongside senior emperors.

[Regencies](/wiki/Regencies "Regencies") (and [coregencies](/wiki/Coregency "Coregency") as a "senior" monarch) are not counted against monarchs, hence [Louis XIV](/wiki/Louis_XIV "Louis XIV") is listed first among the monarchs of sovereign states despite his mother [Anne of Austria](/wiki/Anne_of_Austria "Anne of Austria") being his regent for eight years. A distinction is not made between [absolute](/wiki/Absolute_monarchy "Absolute monarchy") and [constitutional](/wiki/Constitutional_monarchy "Constitutional monarchy") monarchs.

The currently living longest-reigning monarch, [Hassanal Bolkiah](/wiki/Hassanal_Bolkiah "Hassanal Bolkiah") of Brunei, is not included on the list because Brunei was not a sovereign state until 1 January 1984.

In 2002, Blinken was appointed staff director for the [Senate Foreign Relations Committee](/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Foreign_Relations "United States Senate Committee on Foreign Relations"), a position he served in until 2008.[[25]](#cite_note-:0-25) Blinken assisted then-Senator Joe Biden, Chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, in formulating Biden's support for the U.S. invasion of Iraq, with Blinken characterizing the vote to invade Iraq as "a vote for tough diplomacy".[[28]](#cite_note-28) Blinken supported the U.S.-led [invasion of Iraq](/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq "2003 invasion of Iraq") in 2003.[[2]](#cite_note-Joe_Biden's_Vote_for_War-2)[[29]](#cite_note-29)

In the years following the U.S. invasion and occupation of Iraq, Blinken assisted Biden in formulating a proposal in the Senate to establish in Iraq three independent regions divided along ethnic or sectarian lines: a "Shiastan" in the south, a "Sunnistan" in the north, as well as [Iraqi Kurdistan](/wiki/Iraqi_Kurdistan "Iraqi Kurdistan"). The proposal was overwhelmingly rejected at home, as well as in Iraq, where the prime minister opposed the partition plan.[[30]](#cite_note-defender-30)

He was also a senior fellow at the [Center for Strategic and International Studies](/wiki/Center_for_Strategic_and_International_Studies "Center for Strategic and International Studies"). In 2008, Blinken worked for [Joe Biden's presidential campaign](/wiki/Joe_Biden_2008_presidential_campaign "Joe Biden 2008 presidential campaign"),[[5]](#cite_note-twp-5) and was a member of the [Obama–Biden presidential transition](/wiki/Presidential_transition_of_Barack_Obama "Presidential transition of Barack Obama") team.[[31]](#cite_note-LaMonica-31)

Jiang Zemin was born in the city of Yangzhou, Jiangsu, on 17 August 1926.[[1]](#cite_note-3) His ancestral home was the Jiangcun Village (江村) in [Jingde County](/wiki/Jingde_County "Jingde County"), Anhui. This was also the hometown of a number of prominent figures in Chinese academic and intellectual establishments.[[2]](#cite_note-4) Jiang grew up during the years of [Japanese occupation](/wiki/Second_Sino-Japanese_War "Second Sino-Japanese War"). His uncle and foster father, [Jiang Shangqing](/w/index.php?title=Jiang_Shangqing&action=edit&redlink=1 "Jiang Shangqing (page does not exist)"), died fighting the Japanese and was considered in Jiang Zemin's time to be a national hero.[[3]](#cite_note-:322-5): 40 After Shangqing's death, Zemin became his male heir.[[4]](#cite_note-6)

Jiang attended the Department of Electrical Engineering at the [National Central University](/wiki/National_Central_University "National Central University") in Japanese-occupied [Nanjing](/wiki/Nanjing "Nanjing") before transferring to National Chiao Tung University (now [Shanghai Jiao Tong University](/wiki/Shanghai_Jiao_Tong_University "Shanghai Jiao Tong University")). He graduated there in 1947 with a bachelor's degree in [electrical engineering](/wiki/Electrical_engineering "Electrical engineering").[[5]](#cite_note-time_obituary-7) Jiang joined the Chinese Communist Party when he was in college.[[6]](#cite_note-auto-8) After the establishment of the People's Republic of China, Jiang received his training at the [Stalin Automobile Works](/wiki/ZiL "ZiL") in Moscow in the 1950s.[[7]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKuhn200466-9) He also worked for Changchun's [First Automobile Works](/wiki/FAW_Group "FAW Group").[[8]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKuhn2004609-10) As Jiang became increasingly involved in the Communist Party, his main work shifted from the technical side of engineering to administrative and political tasks.[[3]](#cite_note-:322-5): 140
